quotes.text: Learn how to accept BLIK, a common payment method in Poland.
This article has multiple variants. Fetch one of the following URLs to view specific content for your use case:

old_evidence.text: The BLIK code is valid for 2 minutes; customers have 60 seconds to authorize the payment after starting a payment.
`confirmBlikPayment` doesn’t return until the confirmation succeeds or fails.
After confirming the PaymentIntent with valid parameters, the PaymentIntent’s `status` becomes `requires_action`.
After confirmation with valid parameters, the status of the PaymentIntent becomes `requires_action` and `onPaymentResult` is called with `PaymentResult.Completed`.

findings: Semantic raw delta: the November capture is a 17-line index pointing to Checkout, Direct API, iOS and Android variants (new raw lines 5-17; diff lines 3-21 and 1191-1195). The May combined guide already had those four sections (old raw lines 8-10, 196-204, 728-734 and 963-969). A short index does not imply deprecation, changed integration mechanics, SDK support or account eligibility.

Baseline summary accuracy: current source line 28 labels stripe.confirmBlikPayment 'Synchronous' and suggests that not returning until success/failure proves a completed payment. The guide shows an awaited Promise-like call in React (old raw lines 522-566), says Stripe.js polling can be disabled via handleActions false (old raw lines 478 and 522), and then describes PaymentIntent requires_action/next_action blik_authorize with a separate 60-second bank authorization (old raw lines 673-685). Replace the blocking/success implication with an asynchronous confirmation and explicit Intent-status outcome boundary; wiki/concepts/stripe-blik.md line 49 repeats the broad synchronous label.

Baseline summary omits the two-minute code validity beside its 60-second authorization window (source lines 27-30 versus old raw lines 18-20 and 451-457). It also omits Android's PaymentMethodOptionsParams.Blik plus PaymentLauncher route and its Completed-callback-not-payment-success warning (old raw lines 1079-1143), despite naming Android at source lines 13 and 46. iOS succeeded handlerStatus similarly accompanies requires_action, so only subsequent PaymentIntent succeeded confirms the payment (old raw lines 892-914).

The May Checkout compatibility is PLN, payment mode yes, setup/subscription not yet, with PLN Checkout line items; hosted, embedded_page and elements Session examples are distinct UI modes (old raw lines 22-38 and 53-130). The new top-level index has no separate Elements link (new raw lines 13-17), which does not withdraw the May Session example. The old Direct API React Elements provider is optional infrastructure for other methods, while BLIK code collection remains a custom form (old raw lines 308-310 and 358-408).

The dated May guide states 13-month refunds/disputes with no appeal for bank disputes, plus sandbox-only arbitrary six-digit success and email-pattern simulations (old raw lines 145-188, 687-726 and 1163-1190). Those are not November-verified live behavior. The Direct API React code comments say the customer redirects away (old raw lines 573-574 and 641-642), conflicting with the prose no-redirect BLIK code/bank-app flow (old raw lines 18-20 and 478-522); keep the prose-supported method behavior qualified and do not infer a browser redirect from generic sample comments.
historical_claims_to_preserve: May 3, 2026 guide: BLIK single-use six-digit code, two-minute code lifetime, bank-app push approval within 60 seconds, PLN-only Checkout payment mode and same-currency line items (old raw lines 18-38). November only names variants (new raw lines 5-17).

May guide: Checkout hosted, embedded_page and elements Session examples, plus optional description and statement_descriptor display limits in the banking app (old raw lines 53-139). The new index lacks an Elements link, but does not establish removal.

May guide: Direct API creates a server PaymentIntent, returns its client secret, then collects code on client for confirmBlikPayment; requires_action/blik_authorize is an intermediate state and succeeded/payment_intent.succeeded is fulfillment evidence, while payment_failed returns to requires_payment_method (old raw lines 219-239, 308-310, 449-478 and 673-685).

May guide: iOS and Android handler completion can occur while PaymentIntent remains requires_action; poll Intent status and show payment confirmation only on succeeded (old raw lines 892-914 and 1111-1143). Android 23.5.0 and Stripe.js dahlia are dated sample versions (old raw lines 344-353 and 1001-1011).

May guide: sandbox success uses any six digits and failure email patterns cover immediate invalid/expired code, delayed bank/provider declines and 60-second timeouts; 13-month refund and dispute windows have a no-appeal warning (old raw lines 145-188, 687-726 and 1163-1190).
conflicts: Current source line 28 and reciprocal wiki/concepts/stripe-blik.md line 49 call confirmBlikPayment synchronous; old raw lines 478, 522-566 and 673-685 describe an awaited confirmation, optional polling control and a separate requires_action bank step. The phrase risks conflating confirmation result with completed payment.

Current source line 34 says iOS poll succeeded but does not state that the handler's succeeded result can precede actual payment success; old raw lines 892-914 explicitly pair succeeded handlerStatus with requires_action. The Android Completed callback has the same boundary (old raw lines 1120-1143).

Old raw Direct API React comments at lines 573-574 and 641-642 mention redirecting away, whereas old raw lines 18-20 and 478-522 describe code entry and app authorization without a browser redirect; source line 28 and concept line 23 should avoid grounding a universal browser behavior on either generic comment.
unresolved_questions: The November index does not include the linked variant bodies (new raw lines 11-17), so their current UI behavior, requirements, SDK versions and availability are unverified.

findings: Add November index as separately dated navigation and retain May full-guide provenance (new raw lines 9-17; current source lines 4-8 and 44-46). Correct 'Synchronous' to awaited confirmation with a separate requires_action/blik_authorize bank step; state that native handler Completed/succeeded is not PaymentIntent succeeded (current source lines 27-34; old raw lines 478, 673-685, 910-914 and 1139-1143). Add two-minute code validity, Android flow locator and no-appeal dispute warning (old raw lines 18-20, 151-157 and 1079-1143).
conflicts: The relevant wiki/concepts/stripe-blik.md line 49 repeats the broad synchronous description and lines 21-23 present an unconditional no-redirect confirmation, requiring a dated outcome and sample-comment qualification (old raw lines 573-574, 641-642 and 673-685).
source_assessments.reason: The November capture changes navigation only, but independent inspection of the May guide exposes material baseline summary state and timing omissions. A later coordinator source correction is warranted without asserting a current Stripe behavior change.

answers.Q1: At https://docs.stripe.com/payments/blik/accept-a-payment, the complete November capture establishes a four-variant index for Checkout, Direct API, iOS and Android (new raw lines 5-17), not updated payment behavior. The May guide describes a PLN-only single-use six-digit BLIK code valid two minutes, followed by bank-app push approval within 60 seconds; Checkout permits payment mode, not setup or subscription, and requires PLN line items (old raw lines 18-38). Direct API creates a server PaymentIntent and passes its client secret to the client for code confirmation; requires_action with blik_authorize follows valid confirmation, and only later succeeded/payment_intent.succeeded supports fulfillment (old raw lines 219-239, 449-478 and 673-685). iOS and Android handler success/Completed can precede payment success (old raw lines 910-914 and 1139-1143). The mapped source-stripe-blik-accept-payment.md covers the routes and sandbox failures but calls confirmation synchronous and omits that native outcome distinction and code lifetime (current source lines 13-42).
answers.Q2: At https://docs.stripe.com/payments/blik/accept-a-payment, the November difference is presentation/navigation: the new index names four previously documented paths and does not refresh or deprecate the May mechanics (new raw lines 9-17; old raw lines 8-20, 196-204, 728-734 and 963-969). source-stripe-blik-accept-payment.md should retain dated hosted, embedded and Elements Checkout Session examples, PLN/payment-mode constraints, 13-month refund/dispute window with no appeal, and sandbox-only six-digit and email-pattern tests (old raw lines 22-38, 53-188). Its 'synchronous' label should be qualified as an awaited Stripe.js confirmation, since requires_action/blik_authorize and native handler completion precede bank authorization and PaymentIntent succeeded (old raw lines 478-522, 673-685, 910-914 and 1139-1143). The reciprocal stripe-blik concept repeats that label; generic React sample comments about browser redirection conflict with the documented no-redirect code/app flow (wiki/concepts/stripe-blik.md lines 21-23 and 49; old raw lines 573-574). Dated dahlia and Android 23.5.0 examples do not prove current runtime, eligibility or successful settlement.
